title: Evidence retention & traceability runway for Dedicated and Private onboarding
creator: Lena Rodriguez
description:
Objective: create a repeatable evidence mapping and retention runway to accelerate Dedicated and Private customers through SOC2/ISO onboarding while preserving minimal blast radius for data residency and tenant isolation.

Scope: Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (VPC/on-prem) onboarding flows. Work covers: evidence catalog normalization across services (SSO/SAML, audit logging, key management), retention policy templates for multi-tenant vs single-tenant customers, automated export hooks for compliance bundles, and traceability links from customer request -> control -> stored artifact.

Why now: Several inbound enterprise deals are delayed by manual evidence requests and inconsistent retention windows between hosted and private deployments. Standardizing the evidence runway reduces time-to-acceptance, lowers support load, and de-risks sales cycles.

High-level milestones: 
1) Evidence catalog design (owners, artifact types, retention windows, access controls) — deliver confluence schema and mapping table.
2) Traceability model (unique artifact IDs, linkage to onboarding tickets and telemetry) — small schema change + metadata tag conventions.
3) Retention policy templates and automation knobs (per-tenant TTLs, export endpoints) — runtime and Private operator config.
4) Export & bundle generator for auditor delivery — CLI and Console action.
5) Acceptance run with two pilot customers (one Dedicated, one Private) and SOC2 auditor checklist verification.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Confluence evidence catalog published and signed off by Security and Compliance.
- Minimal retained artifact set defined with TTLs per artifact class and code-level guards to enforce retention.
- Export bundle generator produces a signed, tamper-evident archive containing required artifacts for auditors.
- Pilot customer onboarding completed within target SLA (90% of steps automated).
- Runbook for support and SRE with playbooks for evidence requests within Console.

Success metrics: 
- Time to evidence delivery reduced from avg 5 business days to <2 days for pilot customers.
- Number of manual evidence requests from sales/support reduced by 60%.
- Auditor feedback: no major control gaps for evidence traceability during pilot.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: Private/on-prem packaging requires operator-run steps that vary by customer environment. Mitigation: produce clear operator checklist + optional on-site assistance; push critical telemetry into customer-controlled storage endpoints.
- Risk: Retention policies conflict with customer legal requirements. Mitigation: include per-tenant override fields and surface warnings; require customer sign-off for non-default retention.

Next steps (this cycle):
- Finalize evidence catalog draft (owner: Aisha) — due 2026-03-19.
- Align ENG dependencies: ENG-40321 (audit-log indexer), ENG-41102 (export signing) — unblock with engineering scoping session by 2026-03-16.
- Schedule pilot outreach to two customers (solutions + success) and schedule auditor availability.

Notes on implementation trade-offs: prefer lightweight metadata tags and existing storage locations to avoid large migrations; where impossible, add an extraction shim to normalize older artifacts. For Private deployments we accept an operator-assisted step initially with a roadmap to fully-automated bundles in a later release.
